findings.summary: The page claims every result ends in ORDER BY, but most drills in the set have no ORDER BY.
findings.evidence: "Every result ends in **ORDER BY**, so output is deterministic" (Q9, Q10, Q16, Q18, Q19, Q31 and others have none)

findings.summary: The cheatsheet says SELECT aliases work in ORDER BY only, but PostgreSQL also accepts output-column aliases in GROUP BY.
findings.evidence: "Aliases from SELECT work in ORDER BY only"
findings.fix: Write: "SELECT aliases work in ORDER BY (and in PostgreSQL's GROUP BY), but not in WHERE or HAVING."

findings.summary: The tip uses percentile_disc in Q66 before Q66 appears, and it is never otherwise shown.
findings.evidence: "Use percentile_disc(0.5) in Q66 to return an actual salary instead of an average." Q66 is on page 17.
findings.fix: Move the tip to page 17 under Q66 and include a one-line percentile_disc example.

findings.summary: The interview-pattern cheatsheet recommends techniques that differ from the solutions taught.
findings.evidence: "top N per group | ROW_NUMBER + PARTITION BY" while Q65 uses DENSE_RANK. "gaps | LAG or id minus ROW_NUMBER" while Q67 uses generate_series plus an anti join.
findings.fix: Change the cheatsheet to "DENSE_RANK + PARTITION BY (or ROW_NUMBER if ties are dropped)" and "generate_series + anti join".
